ai.description: *Hemidactylus aaronbaueri* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a white belly. Distinctive features include a tuberculate dorsum and a tail with enlarged, pointed scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus aaronbaueri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, strongly keeled tubercles forming a lateral fold along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus aaronbaueri* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats, typically inhabiting moist deciduous forests and rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus aaronbaueri* is a nocturnal gecko that primarily hunts for small arthropods on rock faces and cliff crevices under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus aaronbaueri* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus aaronbaueri* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
